c.tagline: Africa's rhythm capital on the mighty Congo River.

taxi.color: yellow/blue shared taxis; private taxis often unmarked
taxi.fareNote: Meters are rarely used — agree the fare before departure, or book through a ride-hailing app for a fixed upfront price.

emergency.police: 112 (national line exists but response is unreliable; contact your hotel or embassy for help)
emergency.medical: No functioning citywide ambulance dispatch; go directly to a private clinic such as Clinique Ngaliema or Centre Médical de Kinshasa
emergency.note: Emergency response is limited and slow in Kinshasa; keep hotel and embassy contact numbers on hand.

avoid.reason: Avoid outlying communes such as Masina, Ndjili and Camp Luka, especially after dark, due to armed robbery risk, and steer clear of any demonstrations.
Kuluna street-gang robbery, phone-snatching and checkpoint shakedowns are common — use vetted drivers everywhere and never walk at night.

hood_desc: Kinshasa's central business and diplomatic district, packed with embassies, banks, ministries and the presidential palace; the safest, most convenient base for business travelers and first-time visitors.
An expansive, partly upscale commune along the Congo River with Mont Ngaliema park and foreign embassies; suits longer-staying expats, NGO workers and diplomats wanting a quieter, leafier setting.

An industrial and commercial commune along the airport corridor with factories, the FIKIN trade-fair grounds and a cluster of business hotels; practical for travelers with work near the port or industrial zone.
A university and residential commune east of downtown with more affordable lodging; suits budget travelers and those visiting the University of Kinshasa area.
A riverside commune between Gombe and Ngaliema centered on the Kintambo Magasin market; a cheaper, still-central alternative for travelers who want to be near downtown without downtown prices.
lodging: Fleuve Congo Hotel by Blazon Hotels

water.note: Tap water is unsafe for visitors; use bottled or purified water only.

transit.pay: Fares on Transco buses and shared minibuses ('fula-fula') are paid in cash — Congolese francs or small-denomination US dollars — directly to the driver or conductor when boarding or alighting; there is no rechargeable fare card. Ride-hailing apps such as Yango let visitors pay by card or mobile money for a fixed, agreed price.
transit.hours: Buses and shared taxis generally run from around 6:00 to 21:00; services are sparse after dark and there is no dedicated night network, so most visitors arrange a private car or hotel driver after dusk.
transit.note: Traffic is often severe, especially along Boulevard du 30 Juin and the N'djili airport road, so journeys can take much longer than the distance suggests.

train: Kinshasa–Matadi railway (limited freight/passenger service operated by SCTP)
bus: Intercity coaches to Matadi, Kikwit, Bandundu and other provincial towns
ferry: Congo River ferry between Kinshasa (Beach Ngobila) and Brazzaville

transit.m: Shared minibus ('fula-fula') to main road junction, then transfer (30-40 min)
Hotel or private airport transfer car (45-60 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not deeply ingrained but is appreciated; rounding up or leaving roughly 5-10% at restaurants, plus small tips for hotel staff and drivers, is common among visitors.
